statement: A replica CREATE failure publishes REPLICA_CREATE_FAILED only after any created local PartitionService is non-promotable and absent from routable tracking, while retryable failures remain retryable through the existing durable operation-owner redrive from a clean node state; in the five-node MovieLens affinity path no failed schema_operations learner promotes after failure/removal and its target is not reported occupied, with promotion safety, topology budgets, retry timing, and durable REMOVE cleanup unchanged, proven by owner-path red-on-revert scenarios and controlled live fixed/reverted observations.

constraints.statement: If this Quest changes source code, spawn a subagent verifier before audit and git handoff, then record a Solver finding with evidence subagent:<id>.

Every CREATE failure, including deferRetry, must make any created participant runtime non-promotable and remove it from routable local tracking before publishing REPLICA_CREATE_FAILED or CREATION_FAILED; durable FAILED visibility may follow but cannot be the runtime fence.

A CREATE failure explicitly marked deferRetry keeps that typed owner outcome, but its next dispatch starts from a clean node state; do not retain or silently overwrite an old PartitionService and do not add a second runtime-resume subsystem.

Reuse the participant's canonical runtime/resource cleanup primitives and the existing durable REMOVE/replay lifecycle; do not add a second durable deletion authority, trust a SERVICES tombstone as proof a runtime stopped, or weaken startup cleanup debt.
Keep learner promotion proof, voter surplus limits, spread/quorum safety, target occupancy rules, retry cadence, timeouts, numeric budgets, and five-node workload semantics unchanged.

The focused real-owner test must fail on base bytes at a named ordering/liveness assertion because failure is published while the local learner remains promotable, and pass on fixed bytes while proving deferRetry is preserved, redrive cannot duplicate the failed runtime, and canonical REMOVE cleanup remains unchanged.

Because this changes a hot failure path, live validation must compare at least two fixed and two reverted controlled observations at the smallest topology that exercises the same owner boundary; the paid five-node release run is not used as an iteration loop.
